advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or guard) that the composed-budget invariant depends on the `timeout` binary being present, since the `bounded` fallback discards the grant and runs unbounded.
evidence: `clamped` computes a grant then calls `bounded "$want" "$@"` (line 572), but the fallback `bounded` throws `$want` away
The 'BUILD-ENFORCED invariant' comment (lines 99-121) and the deadline math assume `timeout` bounds each call; that assumption is unstated in the degradation branch
advisory.finding: When the `timeout` binary is absent, `bounded(){ shift; "$@"; }` discards the granted duration and runs the command unbounded, which means the entire whole-probe composed-budget invariant (the fix's core mechanism) silently no-ops — there is no signal that budget enforcement is off, so a slow host in this configuration can still be SIGTERM-ed exactly as before.
scenarios: A host without coreutils `timeout` exercising the probe under I/O load — the clamp grant is ignored and calls run unbounded

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider persisting the cold-start-resolved region to REGION_CACHE in the `--report-exit` hook so repeated cold invocations do not re-hit IMDS.
evidence: The main-run path writes REGION_CACHE (lines 220-229) but the hook's cold-start branch does not persist `report_region`
advisory.finding: In the `--report-exit` cold-start path, when a region is resolved from the single-shot IMDS fallback it is used to publish but is never written to REGION_CACHE, so a subsequent hand-invoked or cold hook re-hits IMDS instead of reusing the just-resolved value.
scenarios: A truncation hook firing before any successful main run has cached a region, repeatedly

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the probe_truncated alarm's reliance on treat_missing_data=breaching is acceptable for the cold-start-truncated case where no region is cached and IMDS is unreachable.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:197 `if [ -n "$report_region" ]; then` (metric published only when a region resolves)

The region cache is written by the main run at lines 221-227, after the IMDS block; a run truncated before that point (or before any successful run has cached a region) leaves the hook with no cached region.
advisory.finding: The ExecStopPost truncation-report hook publishes probe_truncated to CloudWatch only when a region resolves from the REGION_CACHE file (/var/lib/rebar/probe-region) or a cold-start IMDS fallback; on a first-ever run that is truncated before the cache is written AND with IMDS unreachable under I/O pressure, probe_truncated never reaches CloudWatch and the alarm can only fire via treat_missing_data=breaching, not on the explicit signal.
scenarios: Cold-start host where the very first probe run is SIGTERM-ed under I/O pressure before REGION_CACHE is written, and IMDS also hangs — probe_truncated is logged to journald but not to CloudWatch.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the --report-exit dispatch stays ahead of all prologue/network code so TimeoutStopSec=15 cannot be violated by future edits (consider a test asserting the branch precedes IMDS).
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:179 `if [ "${1:-}" = "--report-exit" ]; then` — the guard must precede the IMDS prologue at line 210 for the stop path to stay within TimeoutStopSec=15
The change comment (lines 154-161) documents that placing this guard after the IMDS block was 'wrong three times over'.
advisory.finding: ExecStopPost re-invokes the full observability.sh binary on EVERY stop (including successful stops) with --report-exit; correctness of the early-exit guard depends on the `--report-exit` branch being physically first before any prologue, so any future refactor that moves prologue/network calls ahead of the branch dispatch would reintroduce the unbudgeted-stop-path defect this change fixed.
scenarios: A later edit adds initialization above the --report-exit dispatch, causing every service stop to run network prologue under the 15s TimeoutStopSec.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a hook test that seeds REGION_CACHE with a malformed value (e.g. whitespace/invalid chars) and asserts the hook does not invoke `aws` with it and falls back to journald.
evidence: Only two cached-region cases exist: `_hook_env(..., cached_region="us-east-1")` and `cached_region=None` (lines 611, 635, 656).

Added validation line in observability.sh: `case "$report_region" in *[!a-z0-9-]* | '') report_region="" ;;` — no test drives a named violating input such as REGION_CACHE containing `us east 1` or `../evil`.

Transitively covered: a malformed cached region routes into the same cold-start/no-region path that IS tested (test_truncation_hook_reports_to_journald_when_no_region_can_be_resolved), so this is advisory.
advisory.finding: The added region-sanitization on the truncation hook (`case "$report_region" in *[!a-z0-9-]* | '') report_region="" ;;`) is not directly exercised: no test seeds REGION_CACHE with a malformed value (whitespace/invalid characters) to prove a bad cached region is blanked and falls through to the cold-start path rather than being passed to `aws --region`.
scenarios: A stale/corrupt /var/lib/rebar/probe-region file is written by a bug or partial write; the hook must ignore it, not publish to an invalid region.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a hook test invoking `--report-exit` with SERVICE_RESULT unset and assert probe_truncated is published as 0.
evidence: Added source behavior: `probe_result="${SERVICE_RESULT:-success}"` with comment 'It is empty when this is invoked by hand, which reports as untruncated rather than inventing a failure'.
No test invokes `--report-exit` with SERVICE_RESULT absent from the environment to pin probe_truncated=0.
advisory.finding: The `--report-exit` hand-invocation default (`probe_result="${SERVICE_RESULT:-success}"` -> probe_truncated=0 when SERVICE_RESULT is unset) — documented as intentional (the §2e rule) — is not tested; every hook test sets SERVICE_RESULT explicitly (timeout or success).
scenarios: An operator runs `rebar-observability.sh --report-exit` by hand with no SERVICE_RESULT; the contract says it must report untruncated (0), not fabricate a failure.
